skill.name: payoff-action-modeling
skill.description: Model post-outcome UI actions from user intent. Use it to decide which actions to show, hide, group, label, prioritize, and place after a user completes a meaningful workflow.
skill.summary: Turn completed product workflows into clear, scoped, and prioritized UI action models.
skill.author: JohnWayneeee

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The backtick detections are Markdown inline terms, the URL is a passive reference link, and the blocker matches are normal design guidance. No semantic security findings or prompt injection attempts were found.

static_findings.snippet: - `Primary outcome`: the result, resource, state, or completion the user should understand first.
- `Outcome state type`: `completion`, `generation`, `workspace`, `review`, `handoff`, `recovery`, or
- `User questions`: realistic "What if I want to..." questions from the user's point of view.
- `Action scope`: `outcome`, `selection`, `item`, `continuation`, `navigation`, `recovery`, or `assi
- `Intent pressure`: `immediate`, `contextual`, or `deferred`.
- `UI placement`: `primary CTA`, `secondary action`, `per-item action`, `row menu`, `accordion detai
- `Required vs optional`: whether the action must be visible now or can be deferred.
- `Copy`: short labels written as user-facing outcomes, not implementation details.
- `immediate`: the user probably needs this action now to capture value or finish the job.
- `contextual`: the action matters when the user is inspecting a specific object, state, error, or s
- `deferred`: the action is useful but should not compete with the primary outcome moment.
- `Create another`, `Generate more`, `Import more`, `Add teammate`, `Publish`, `Run again`, `Open wo
- `outcome`: affects the full result, resource set, completed flow, report, upload, import, deployme
- `selection`: affects multiple chosen objects or resources.
- `item`: affects one row, card, file, record, task, case, page, comment, or resource.
- `continuation`: extends, repeats, branches, adds to, or continues the workflow.
- `navigation`: moves across screens, workspaces, dashboards, sources, projects, or settings.
- `recovery`: supports undo, retry, restore, compare, history, rollback, discard, or error repair.
- `assistance`: supports help, explanation, AI refinement, recommendations, support, or guided impro

- Use `Export` when the user must configure format, columns, mapping, destination, permissions, or i

- Use `Review selected`, `Approve selected`, `Download selected`, `Move selected`, `Merge selected`,
- Use `Create another`, `Generate more`, `Import more`, `Upload more`, `Run again`, `Sync again`, `A
- Use `Back to source`, `Back to plan`, `Back to settings`, `Open dashboard`, or `Go to workspace` w

- Showing a global `Edit` action when editing happens per item.
- Mixing `Export`, `Save`, and `Download` ambiguously.
- Using unclear scope labels such as `Download` when the action affects all items.
- Using `Export` as the main CTA when the user thinks in terms of downloading a ready result.
- Adding `Generate more`, `Import more`, `Run again`, or `Create another` as a required onboarding s

content.value_statement: Product teams often overload success states with unclear next steps. This skill turns user intent into scoped, prioritized UI actions after a meaningful outcome.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the primary outcome and outcome state type for completed workflows.
Generates user-intent questions across item, selection, outcome, navigation, recovery, and assistance scopes.
Classifies actions by scope, intent pressure, required status, and UI placement.
Recommends clear labels for CTAs, row actions, bulk toolbars, menus, and next screens.
Checks action models for density, recovery, scope separation, and label clarity.
limitations: Does not implement UI components or production code.
Requires product context to produce specific and useful actions.
Does not replace usability testing, analytics, or customer research.
Provides design guidance, not compliance or accessibility certification.

use_cases.title: Clarify a completion screen
use_cases.description: Decide the primary CTA, secondary actions, and recovery options after onboarding, import, setup, or publishing is complete.

use_cases.title: Structure generated-result actions
use_cases.description: Place actions for generated reports, files, recommendations, or test cases without hiding inspection and refinement paths.

use_cases.title: Audit workflow action density
use_cases.description: Review whether a dashboard, review state, or handoff flow exposes too many actions at the same moment.

prompt_templates.title: Model a Basic Success State
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a first action model for one completed workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use payoff-action-modeling for this success state: [describe outcome]. Identify the primary action, secondary actions, and recovery options.

prompt_templates.title: Map Actions by Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: separate one-item, selected-item, and full-result actions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use payoff-action-modeling to classify actions for [screen]. Separate outcome, item, selection, continuation, navigation, recovery, and assistance scopes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Action Labels
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: refine copy and placement for confusing actions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use payoff-action-modeling to review these action labels: [labels]. Recommend clearer labels, placements, and required versus optional status.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate action density across a multi-step product flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use payoff-action-modeling to audit this workflow after completion: [workflow details]. Flag scope conflicts, overloaded tiers, and missing recovery paths.

output_examples.input: A user imports customer records and sees a completion screen with import results.
output: Primary outcome: records imported with a clear summary of accepted and failed rows.
Primary action: Review import. Place row fixes near failed records and put Import more as an optional branch.
Recovery: provide retry, download error file, and field mapping correction near the error state.

output_examples.input: A report generator creates a finished report with charts and recommendations.
output: Primary outcome: report generated and ready to inspect or share.
Primary action: Share report. Keep chart-level explain, edit, and download actions close to each chart.
Deferred actions: schedule, compare versions, and create another report should not compete with the main result.

output_examples.input: A deployment finishes and the product asks what actions should appear next.
output: Primary outcome: deployment completed with status, environment, and timestamp visible.
Primary action: Open deployment. Keep logs, rollback, promote, and retry close to deployment details.
Navigation: provide a quieter path back to project or settings without competing with the main action.

best_practices: Start with the user-visible outcome before listing actions.
Keep item actions near the object they affect.
Make destructive, retry, undo, and restore paths clear when risk exists.
anti_patterns: Do not make every possible action visible at once.
Do not use one vague action label for different scopes.
Do not force continuation after the user has already completed the workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create an action model for product UI states after a meaningful user outcome.

faq.question: Can it design full screens?
faq.answer: It can guide action placement and hierarchy, but it does not produce complete visual UI designs.

faq.question: Is it only for AI products?
faq.answer: No. It also applies to CRUD tools, dashboards, imports, uploads, admin panels, and workflow products.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the completed workflow, visible result, user goals, available objects, risks, and candidate actions.

faq.question: How does it handle destructive actions?
faq.answer: It recommends contextual placement, clear labels, confirmation, recovery, undo, restore, or history when needed.

faq.question: Can it help with action labels?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends labels that describe user outcomes and clarify whether actions affect one item or all items.
